turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Mrs Iyer, please sit. I checked you just outside — BP is 102 over 64, pulse is 108, and saturation is 97 percent. Doctor is coming.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thank you. I'm Dr Menon. You've come with your mother, that's alright. What is troubling you the most?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Doctor, I am very tired. And I get breathless also. I don't know since when exactly, some months...
[SEG0004] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She is not herself. Even sweeping the hall, she sits down in between.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): This breathlessness — on walking, or even when you are sitting?
[SEG0006] person_3 (PATIENT): On the stairs. Our flat is on the second floor, I have to stop halfway. If I am sitting, I am alright, I think.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the tiredness, is it the whole day or only by evening?
[SEG0008] person_3 (PATIENT): Whole day, doctor. I am in accounts, I have cut down to half day because I...
[SEG0009] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Because she was dozing at the desk. Even her boss noticed.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any pain in the chest when you get breathless?
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): No. No chest pain.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any fever or chills?
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): No fever.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Your GP has written that the periods are heavy. Since when is that?
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): Since about one year. They are very heavy only. I don't know, doctor, it just became like this.
[SEG0016] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): One year? No, it was already there before the monsoon last year. One and a half years, minimum.
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): Maybe. I can't remember the month. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright, we won't force a date — somewhere between a year and a year and a half. On a heavy day, how many pads do you use?
[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): I lose count. Six, seven... sometimes more than that. I don't know the exact number.
[SEG0020] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And at night she is getting up to change, two times at least.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Are you passing clots?
[SEG0022] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes. Big clots. Like a coin, sometimes bigger — I don't know how to say the size.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any dizziness, or have you blacked out?
[SEG0024] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Not really. Nothing like that.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): At the desk your mother mentioned the hair. What was—
[SEG0026] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Falling, doctor. Every morning the pillow has hair on it. I told her months back to come.
[SEG0027] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes, when I oil it or wash, it comes out in my hand. Since a few months, I think. I don't know if it is connected.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Are you on any tablets just now?
[SEG0029] person_3 (PATIENT): Iron, sometimes. Ferrous sulphate, the red tablets.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): What dose, and are you taking it every day?
[SEG0031] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The box is just sitting in the cupboard. I keep telling her and still—
[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. Maybe 200 milligrams. Some days I take it, some days I forget. Not daily.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): So ferrous sulphate, possibly 200 mg, and not regular. Was anything else given for the bleeding, tranexamic acid or—
[SEG0034] person_3 (PATIENT): Tranexamic acid, yes. I stopped it in March.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you remember the dose, and why you stopped?
[SEG0036] person_3 (PATIENT): 500 mg, three times a day, only on the heavy days. My stomach was not agreeing, so I left it. I don't know if it was even helping.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): The old letter also mentions norethisterone. Did you take that?
[SEG0038] person_3 (PATIENT): No. They wrote it, but I never took it, not even one tablet. I got worried about hormones, so...

[SEG0039] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Her sister Priya takes biotin gummies for her hair. Should we get the same for her? And my own sister — this girl's aunt — has thyroid, she is on thyroxine 50 micrograms.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): Biotin is Priya's medicine, we are not starting that. The thyroid in your aunt is worth noting. Do you have any thyroid problem yourself?
[SEG0041] person_3 (PATIENT): No, I don't think so. Nobody has checked. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any allergy to a medicine, or to anything else?
[SEG0043] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Nothing that I know of.

[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me examine you. Conjunctiva and tongue are pale, the lungs are clear with no wheeze or crackles, and the heart sounds are normal though the rate is fast. Abdomen is soft, I feel no mass, and there is no swelling at the ankles.
[SEG0045] person_3 (PATIENT): Doctor, one thing I didn't say. When I get up from the bed quickly I do feel dizzy, for a few seconds. I said no earlier, but it happens. I don't know if it matters.
[SEG0046] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She doesn't tell things straight. I have seen her catch the wall.
[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): So light-headed when you stand, for a few seconds. Did you ever actually faint, or only that?
[SEG0048] person_3 (PATIENT): No fainting. Only that light, spinning kind of feeling, then it passes.

[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me say it back, and stop me if I am wrong. You are tired through the day, breathless on the stairs, periods heavy for about a year to a year and a half with many pads and clots, your hair is falling, and you get dizzy on standing. You take iron only sometimes, you stopped tranexamic acid in March, your aunt has thyroid, and there is no chest pain, no fever, no known allergy.
[SEG0050] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes, that is right. Only, the breathlessness — when it started I really don't know, doctor. Maybe three months, maybe longer.

[SEG0051] person_2 (DOCTOR): We'll leave that start date open. My working thought is anaemia from the blood loss, low iron, but I cannot rule out a thyroid problem as well, with the hair fall and the family history.
[SEG0052] person_3 (PATIENT): Anaemia means the blood is less, no? Is it serious?
[SEG0053] person_2 (DOCTOR): It can certainly make you this tired. I will not call it confirmed until we see the tests. I am arranging a full blood count, a ferritin, and a TSH.
[SEG0054] person_1 (NURSE): I am still outside the curtain, doctor. I can take the samples once the form is signed.
[SEG0055] person_2 (DOCTOR): Please take them today. A pelvic scan we might arrange if the bleeding is still this heavy after the blood results — I am not booking it now.
[SEG0056] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And the tranexamic, you want her to start it again?
[SEG0057] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not today. For the iron I am writing ferrous sulphate 200 mg once a day, after food, every day, so the old strip doesn't confuse things.
[SEG0058] person_3 (PATIENT): Once a day, okay. If I become worse before that...
[SEG0059] person_2 (DOCTOR): If you get chest pain, if you faint, or if a pad is soaking through every hour, go to emergency the same day. Otherwise I will see you in two weeks with the reports.
[SEG0060] person_3 (PATIENT): Two weeks. I will ask for leave. I don't know if my manager will...
[SEG0061] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I will bring her, you don't worry about the leave.
[SEG0062] person_1 (NURSE): Come along, Mrs Iyer, we will draw the blood in the next room.

spec.situation: Tired, breathless woman with heavy periods for a year; counts pads and clots in vague terms; takes iron 'sometimes'; hair loss; relative mentions thyroid in the family. Blood tests, maybe pelvic scan.
features: stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.

denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.

third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.

bad.reason: Tiredness and all-day frequency supported; duration 'some months' was stated for symptoms generally, not clearly tiredness alone.
bad.text: Tiredness (category=constitutional, status=present, duration=some months, frequency=throughout the day, temporality=current, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

bad.reason: Doctor prescribed ferrous sulphate 200 mg once daily after food; indication 'iron supplementation' not explicitly stated.
bad.text: Ferrous sulphate (generic_name=ferrous sulfate, dose=200 mg, frequency=once daily, indication=iron supplementation, status=planned, reported_by=doctor)

omissions.text: Breathlessness is absent at rest/sitting; patient said she is alright when sitting.
Heavy bleeding includes needing to get up at night to change pads at least twice.

Initial denial of dizziness/blacking out was revised: patient said no blackout/fainting but later reported brief light-headed/spinning dizziness on standing quickly, lasting a few seconds and then passing.
Tranexamic acid was stopped in March because it upset her stomach ('my stomach was not agreeing'), and patient was unsure it was helping.
Norethisterone was prescribed previously but the patient never took it at all because she was worried about hormones.
Patient denied known thyroid disease in herself, though she said nobody has checked.
Doctor asked for blood samples to be taken today.
Doctor specifically advised not to restart tranexamic acid today.
